en: The Apadāna of the Elder Ticampakapupphiya Thomakavagga 4 I offered three campaka flowers to the Buddha, the Teacher, who was endowed with the marks of a Great Man. Because of that deed, I have been reborn in the world of the gods for eighty-four thousand aeons. Having passed away from there, I was reborn here in the human world. Possessing a beautiful form, I am now a monk in the dispensation of the Buddha Kassapa. I have attained the fruit of Stream-entry; I am one who has reached the goal. I shall attain Parinibbāna before long. This is my final birth. I have no further existence. This is my last body. I am free from all suffering. I have transcended all states of woe. I have crossed over the ocean of saṃsāra. I have reached the further shore. I have attained the supreme security of Nibbāna. I am one who has reached the goal. I shall attain Parinibbāna before long. This is my final birth. I have no further existence. This is my last body. I am free from all suffering. I have transcended all states of woe. I have crossed over the ocean of saṃsāra. I have reached the further shore.

Not far from the Himavat mountain is a peak named Vikata;
The ascetic has cultivated his faculties.
with a serene mind, [one should pay homage].
Having taken three campaka flowers, I scattered them.
Because I offered that flower in worship,
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.
[as above] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Ticampakapupphiya spoke these verses.
This is the fourth legend of the elder Ticampakapupphiya.
